# Known data-quality windows

Date ranges over which a published artifact is known to carry a **measured**
defect that has been **ruled on** and deliberately left in place. This is not
a backlog: an issue is opened to be closed, while a window is a permanent
property of data already on S3 and is meant to be read by whoever reads
those dates.

A window is admitted only when the defect is measured with durable evidence,
the affected data is already published and staying published, and a
disposition has been ruled. A defect still being fixed forward belongs in the
backlog until the forward fix lands; what the fix cannot reach belongs here.

**Register:** `data_quality/windows.py` is authoritative — this file is
rendered from it. Consumers should call
`data_quality.overlapping(artifact, start, end)` rather than reading this
page, so that a run over affected dates refuses or attaches the caveat
without depending on a human having read it.

## `unsettled-session-bar-2026`

The trading day's bar was fetched ~16:06 ET, about 1.5 hours before the consolidated tape settles, so Close and Volume are the vendor's unsettled intraday snapshot rather than the official session values.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Affected dates** | 2026-05-01 through 2026-09-22 |
| **Artifacts** | `features/{date}/technical.parquet`<br>`features/{date}/interaction.parquet`<br>`features/{date}/alternative.parquet`<br>`features/{date}/macro.parquet`<br>`features/{date}/fundamental.parquet`<br>`staging/daily_closes/{date}.parquet`<br>`market_data/eod_closes/{date}.json` |
| **tickers compared** | 920 of 920 |
| **Close drift (median)** | 2.7 bps |
| **Close drift (max)** | 16.4 bps |
| **Volume shortfall (median)** | 20.5 % |
| **Volume shortfall (worst names)** | ~40 % |
| **Evidence** | s3://alpha-engine-research/data_collection/parity/2026-09-21.json — the same-day shadow parity report that first graded the unsettled bar against the settled one |
| **Disposition** | `no_remediation` — ruled by Brian on 2026-09-22 |
| **Re-exam trigger** | The first time a GRADED result depends on these dates: a champion/challenger arm registered from a scoring run whose window includes them, a predictor training window drawn from features/{date} rather than from ArcticDB, or a v2 phase-4/5 backtest gating a promotion. |

- Forward fix landed 2026-09-22 (nousergon-data PR1863, PR1867, PR1868): the standalone EOD collection fires at 18:15 ET, and dates.assert_settled_bar refuses a D03/D19 write whose trading-day row was fetched before settlement. This window is the historical residue that fix cannot reach.
- ArcticDB — and therefore crucible-predictor — is NOT affected beyond a single overnight. weekly_collector._should_skip_morning_enrich skips only when target_date < arctic_last_date, so the D+1 07:30 ET Polygon T+1 overwrite always runs and restores the settled row. Exposure is bounded at roughly 16:06 ET on D to 07:30 ET on D+1.
- Known readers of the dated feature-store artifacts, measured 2026-09-22: crucible-research scoring/factor_scoring.py, scoring/universe_board.py, data/fetchers/feature_store_reader.py, data/scanner_orchestrator.py; crucible-dashboard views/13_Feature_Store.py (display only).
- A remediation, if it is ever ruled, must rewrite the affected dated prefixes from the settled price cache AND write a backfilled_at marker beside each rewritten prefix — a re-derived artifact that is indistinguishable from an original one destroys the reproducibility of every run that read the original.
